text:
maya: quick sync — we need to lock the toolkit scope for the next sprint. customer asks from AcmeHealth + Novatek landed: auto-batching presets, per-route cache TTL + invalidation API, and workload-aware quantization recommendations. can we fit all 3?

zack: probably not all in one sprint. runtime team can deliver batching presets + basic cache hooks. quant recs need eval infra + offline analysis, longer.

riya: we should prioritize based on customer impact. AcmeHealth is blocking a pilot if we don't ship cache invalidation. Novatek cares most about cost (quant). proposal: ship batching + cache small-surface in sprint 1, quant recs in sprint 2 with an alpha.

oliver: +1 to prioritizing cache for AcmeHealth. also we need eval-triggered alerting for any quant rollout — they want auto-detect quality regressions. that requires an eval baseline + signal thresholds.

sam: from UX: cache TTL UI and an invalidate button are straightforward. for quant recs we need an explain panel (why pick int8 vs q4_0) — can be deferred.

zack: technical constraints:
```
- batching: requires continuous-batching + per-route window config (ETA: 3 dev days)
- cache hooks: expose API + eviction event (ETA: 4 dev days)
- quant recs: offline eval pipeline + model fingerprinting (ETA: 3 wks)
```

maya: thanks. so sprint1 scope = batching presets + cache API + minimal UI. sprint2 = quant advisor + eval-alerts. need acceptance criteria for sprint1.

riya: acceptance for sprint1:
- batching: default presets (low/medium/high) applied per-route, no perf regression >5% p50 p99 on existing traffic
- cache: per-route TTL, invalidate endpoint, audit log entries for invalidations
- rollout: canary to 2 pilots (AcmeHealth + internal) for 1 week

oliver: add monitoring SLOs: p95 latency must stay within 1.2x baseline, request queue length < 2x for 99% of 5m windows. add unit eval set sanity checks (smoke prompts) run on canary.

sam: UI acceptance: TTL control + invalidate button in route settings, tooltip with recommended TTLs. add copy for docs.

zack: risk notes: cache invalidation semantics are tricky with prefix caching and shared KV. will implement strong consistency option behind feature flag. also quant recs can cause model divergence — need eval gating.

maya: gating + rollout plan for sprint1:
1) feature-flag rollout to internal -> smoke tests -> enable for AcmeHealth canary -> monitor eval smoke set + infra metrics -> open to wider alpha
2) stop conditions: p50 latency regressions >10% or error rate spike >0.5% for 5m window

riya: for sprint2 quant advisor gating, propose automated eval-triggered alerts with thresholds:
- delta in mean token logprob > 0.5
- n-gram overlap drop > 3% on evaluation set
- false-positive tolerance target < 5% (we'll tune)

oliver: we should store historical evals per customer-route so alerts can be customer-specific. retention 90d.

sam: doc request: will need a short FAQs page about cache semantics + recommended batching presets. i'll draft once we lock scope.

zack: timeline check: sprint1 work estimate = 2 devs x 2 weeks + 1 QA x 1 week. blockers: infra quota for additional KV, and small schema change for audit logs.

maya: can we reduce scope to hit the sprint if infra quota is delayed?

zack: fallback: ship batching presets + TTL UI that uses local in-process cache (no KV) for immediate pilot, then add KV-backed eviction in sprint2. tradeoff: less durable across replicas.

riya: accept fallback as a landing patch if AcmeHealth needs it sooner. note in roadmap and call out in docs.

maya: final ask: owners.
- batching: zack
- cache API + fallback UI: zack + sam for UI
- docs + customer comms: riya
- eval-smoke + alerts spec: oliver

deploy-bot: build 1770008910 passed for branch feat/toolkit-batching (CI: 18m) :thumbsup:

maya: cool. I’ll update the roadmap and timeline with these owners and send an invite for a 30m kick-off tomorrow 10am. thanks all :tada:
